meta.title: Our Pen-Pal Cards
meta.textType: story: an interview for a pen-pal card

paragraphs: On Thursday, October eighth, at one o'clock, the Explorers met in the school library. Teacher Kim gave each child a pen-pal card for Ms. Ong's class. The card had four lines: "First name," "Age," "Hobbies," and "A normal day." "Please fill in your card," said Teacher Kim. "Ask a friend some questions, and write the answers." She wrote an example on the board: "First name: Kim. Hobbies: reading and the violin."

Lily and Mia sat at a table with their cards. "What is your first name?" asked Lily. "My first name is Mia," said Mia, "and I am eleven." "What are you interested in?" asked Lily. "I am interested in animals," said Mia. "I collect animal stickers." "Have you ever played chess?" asked Lily. "No, never," said Mia, and she smiled. "What else do you do?" asked Lily. "I like to dance, and I practice every day," said Mia. "What is a normal day for you?" asked Lily. "I get up at six, and I walk to school with you!" said Mia. Lily laughed and wrote the answers on the card.

May asked Leo the same kind of questions. "Have you ever played in a team?" asked May. "Yes, I have," said Leo. "I played football in a team last year." "Do you play an instrument?" asked May. "I have never played an instrument," said Leo. "But my pencil is a good drum." Then Leo wrote "Leo, aged one hundred" on his card, and he grinned. Teacher Kim looked at it. "A true card, please," she said. Leo laughed and wrote "eleven."

Then Teacher Kim put a box on the table. It said, "FOR MS. ONG'S CLASS." The children put their cards in the box. "I hope Grace likes my card," said Lily. "Every normal day is a good story," said Teacher Kim.
